clusters.name: Teodor's death, 1978–1979
clusters.reason: Around your grandfather Teodor's death in January 1978, within the following year: your grandmother Delphine stopped cooking and went to your mother's every evening; your father took night shifts and distanced from your mother; your uncle Anton drank at lunch and separated from his wife; your mother lay awake over them; and your brother Callum had ear infections through the winter. Your grandmother took a job at the library by May 1979 and her functioning rose, settling the period.

clusters.name: Odette's pregnancy bed rest, 1984–1984
clusters.reason: Around your mother being ordered to bed for pregnancy in March 1984, within the following months: your grandmother Hazel came every morning to keep house and overfunctioned; your father argued with her over how she kept it; your brother Callum stammered again; and your sister Ines was born in September. The shifts pile up in the same months as the constraint on your mother's functioning, and they settle once she delivered.

clusters.name: Hazel's Parkinson's diagnosis, 1986–1997
clusters.reason: Around your grandmother Hazel's diagnosis with Parkinson's disease in September 1986, over the following eleven years: your grandfather Ambrose took over her cooking and appointments and overfunctioned; your father phoned him every night and his anxiety rose; Hazel had a bad fall in 1988 and her functioning fell, then rose briefly with new medicine; your father and uncle Lyle argued over who should help their parents; your grandfather's chest pains began; Hazel could no longer dress herself by 1991 and your father took her to the clinic twice a week; your aunt Mavis came to stay to nurse her sister; your father drank most evenings; your aunt Pearl had panic spells at the wheel; Hazel could no longer stand by 1995 and your grandfather gave up his workshop and hardly left her side; your father fought with your mother over his evenings at his parents' house. Hazel moved into the Fairlie nursing home in June 1997, settling this long period.

clusters.name: Callum leaving home, 1999–2000
clusters.reason: Around your brother Callum leaving home in May 1999 for a job up north, within the following year: your father and Callum argued most nights over his plans; your mother could not settle at the thought of him so far away and her anxiety rose; your father missed days at work and sat up late in the garage; your sister Ines skipped school most of that autumn and her functioning fell; your mother took Ines with her everywhere; and by August 2000 Ines was back at school full days and passed her exams. The shifts settle once Ines's functioning rose.

clusters.name: Hazel's death, 2003–2003
clusters.reason: Around your grandmother Hazel's death in January 2003, within the following year: you could not sleep more than a few hours a night; you stopped going in to the bookshop and were let go in May; you dreaded buses and crowded shops and went out only after dark; your anxiety rose. By November 2003 you took a job at the garden centre and were sleeping through the night again. Every shift in these months is yours, and no one else's shows then.
